title: Projects
summary: reconcile fluid project folders, Project notes, and historical Studio source paths through four bounded Docs Viewer deliveries
content_html:
Projects

Purpose

Give current, historical, and prospective project folders a flexible notes layer, and replace the Studio Project State pipeline with Docs Viewer reconciliation while keeping Studio Works stable catalogue records.

The feature keeps three deliberately different worlds visible:

world role
Studio strict database owner of Works, Series, publishing workflow, and recorded source-path history
Docs Viewer semi-structured owner of Project notes and optional convenience links, which may drift
folders fluid human working world with no canonical identity or enforced lifecycle

Project State observes disagreement among them. It does not make one system manage the other two.

PRJ-1 and PRJ-2 are entirely Docs Viewer-owned and do not change Studio. PRJ-3 is the narrow integration exception: Project State reads the existing Work fields through a Studio-read-only post-commit observer, but it never adds folder_path to Studio, rewrites Work data, or participates in Studio's catalogue workflow.

Feature Documents

  • Projects Concept — the three-world model, Project-document meaning, three-way reconciliation, local-link experience, Resolver Token purpose, invariants, and non-goals.
  • Local File And Folder Links Concept — base-relative local targets, dlf-local: Markdown links, focused paste conversion, confined Manage activation, and inert public projection.
  • Projects Architecture — authority boundaries, folder_path projection, path normalization and activation, Project State snapshots, targeted refresh, resolver lookup, and retirement contracts.
  • PRJ-1 — Docs Viewer Local Folder Links Delivery — completed: normalize Finder-style paths into safe clickable local links and provide confined Manage-only activation plus inert public projection.
  • PRJ-2 — Projects Customisation And Apple Notes Migration Delivery — completed: Projects-only folder_path metadata and manifest data plus the exact-plan migration of the dated Apple Notes project corpus.
  • PRJ-3 — Docs Viewer Project State Delivery — build the three-way report and resolver lookup, add targeted refresh hooks, and retire Studio's Project State machinery.
  • PRJ-4 — Resolver Tokens Delivery — render bounded one-hop related-item lists from Project State data without scans, chaining, or a global relationship graph.

Delivery Order

order delivery complete outcome
1 PRJ-1 — Docs Viewer Local Folder Links A pasted Finder or terminal path becomes a marked base-relative link: clickable through confined local Manage and inert in public output.
2 PRJ-2 — Projects Customisation And Apple Notes Migration Project documents own optional folder_path metadata in their local Manage manifest, and a checked-in one-off command imports the reviewed Apple Notes corpus without inventing folder matches.
3 PRJ-3 — Docs Viewer Project State One Docs Viewer report reconciles current folders, Project documents, and historical Works while publishing the Project resolver lookup and retiring the Studio implementation.
4 PRJ-4 — Resolver Tokens Any permitted managed document can expand one exact folder or Work subject into its precomputed one-hop Project relationships.

The deliveries are sequential. PRJ-2 consumes PRJ-1's path contract. PRJ-3 consumes PRJ-2's structured Manage-manifest projection. PRJ-4 begins only after the Project State lookup, refresh, failure, and access contracts work independently through the report.

Feature Boundary

In scope:

  • ordinary body links for local folder paths;
  • one optional Project-document folder_path convenience field;
  • no Studio dependency for local links or Project-document metadata;
  • $DOTLINEFORM_PROJECTS_BASE_DIR as the containment boundary for local links, while projects/ remains the Project discovery and reconciliation area;
  • a registered Manage-only Projects sub-scope customisation;
  • a write-free plan and exact create-only apply for the dated Apple Notes project export;
  • three-way, read-only Docs Viewer reconciliation;
  • targeted post-commit updates plus explicit full refresh;
  • retirement of the existing Studio Project State route and static report; and
  • bounded one-hop Resolver Tokens backed by Project State data.

Not in scope:

  • a canonical folder registry or folder/document synchronization;
  • automatic rename, move, merge, repair, or deletion;
  • use of folder_path by Studio's media or publishing workflows;
  • adding folder_path to Works or mapping it onto project_folder;
  • continuation of the old primary-image audit;
  • recursive relationship chaining or a global graph database; or
  • public activation of local targets or public projection of Project relationship data.

Existing Baseline

Project State describes the current Studio route and generated Markdown implementation. Sub-Scope Report Customisation Architecture owns the shipped default/customisation seam extended by PRJ-2. Docs Viewer Reports owns the local report boundary that PRJ-3 will use.

PRJ-1 and PRJ-2 are complete. PRJ-3 is next. The shipped local-link and Projects customisation contracts route to their durable architecture owners; the retained PRJ-2 record owns migration evidence and reconciliation gaps.
